_doc: PHASE_2_NAVIGATION_AND_GATHERING.md §2.0 — grid extent per context.
home: fixed. Wave 17 #6 widened this from 56 to 200 (== WORLD_HALF,
data/world.ts) — the six GROUNDS a villager actually hauls to/from
(grounds.generated.json) scatter nodes up to ~197m from origin
(ironseam's far corner), so a 56m grid left every real haul entirely
outside it: findPath() bails out (out-of-bounds endpoint) and navSteer
falls back to a raw beeline for the whole trip, no road preference, no
obstacle avoidance, past the player's own buildings. 200m covers the
worst case with margin and matches the world edge, so it never falls
short again as grounds move. The one region this widened grid must NOT
make walkable is The Downs (data/downs.ts) — a sloped-terrain prototype
every home-world walker still draws at hardcoded y=0 — so it is fenced
off with a static 'blocked' entry in navTerrain.ts's
terrainExclusions, the same mechanism that already keeps the pond
unpathable, rather than by relying on grid extent as before.
destination: window, a 96m (2x halfExtent) box that follows the player
through a template diorama rather than covering the whole declared
radius (213-352m across the nine templates — see PHASE_STATUS.md's
corrected gap #1). recentreAt is the hysteresis distance: rebuild only
once the player has moved this far from the window's current centre,
not every frame.
crypt: fixed, but sized per-descent from the generated room layout, not
from a static number here — see iteration 2.6.
maxStep is read by iteration 2.5's height rasterization, not yet by
anything in iteration 2.4 — declared here now so both iterations read
the same number rather than each hardcoding their own.
